lessons.title: Holidays
goals: 🗓️ Ask and answer 'How do you celebrate?'
📅 Describe what people do on special days
warmup: Name 3 holidays in Uzbekistan. / O'zbekistondagi 3 ta bayramni ayting.
How do you celebrate Nowruz? / Navro'zni qanday nishonlaysiz?

x: We celebrate Eid with our family.
I give gifts to my friends.
The guests arrive in the morning.

grammar.rule: **How do you celebrate...? / We usually... + traditions**
ex: We **usually visit** our grandparents and **cook** sumalak.
Biz odatda buvijonnikiga boramiz va sumalak pishiramiz.

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: On Eid we ___ our relatives. → a) visit b) visiting c) visited

reading.title: Nowruz in Our Home
reading.passage: Nowruz is the most important holiday in our family. A week before, we clean the whole house and decorate the rooms with flowers. On the day, my grandmother cooks sumalak in a big pot — she starts at night and stirs it until morning! Our relatives come as guests, and we eat plov together. Children receive gifts and play outside. At night, we watch fireworks over the city. I love Nowruz because everyone is together.
qs: What does the family do a week before Nowruz?
What does grandmother cook?
What do children receive?
Why does the writer love Nowruz?

listening.title: Eid Morning
qs: What time does the family get up?
Where do they go in the morning?
What do the children get?
listening.script: Listen. On Eid morning, we get up very early — at five o'clock. We put on our new clothes and go to the mosque. Then we visit our grandparents. We have a big breakfast with plov. The children get gifts and new clothes. In the afternoon, friends come to visit us. It is a happy day.

writing.title: My Favourite Holiday
writing.task: Write a paragraph (5-7 sentences) about your favourite holiday: what people do, what you eat, who comes.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: We cook sumalak and visit relatives.
What do you eat on Eid?
Navruz, because I see my cousins.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Ask your parents about an old family tradition and tell the class. / Ota-onangizdan an'ana haqida so'rang.

quiz: What do you usually eat on holidays?
lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 holiday words 3× · Grammar: 6 sentences about your favourite holiday · Reading: re-read 'Nowruz in Our Home' · Speaking: describe a holiday to your family.
teacher: Anchor lesson for the Strong A2 band.
Let students share real holiday memories — high motivation.

lessons.title: Travel and Transport
goals: 🎫 Buy a ticket and read a timetable
Bilet sotib olish va jadval o'qish
warmup: Name 5 ways to travel. / 5 ta transport ayting.
Which is faster: plane or train? / Nima tezroq?

x: I need two tickets to Samarkand.

grammar.rule: **Travel expressions:** It takes + time · depart/arrive at + time · by plane/train/bus

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: Which is faster? → a) A plane is faster than a train b) A train is faster than a plane

reading.title: To Samarkand by Train
reading.passage: Last summer we travelled to Samarkand by train. We checked the timetable and bought tickets for the morning express. The train departed at 8:30 from platform 2. The journey took four hours. We watched the fields and mountains pass by the window. At noon we arrived at Samarkand station. The city was waiting for us — blue domes, kind people, and delicious bread.
qs: How did the family travel to Samarkand?
When did the train depart?
How long did the journey take?
What did they see from the window?

listening.title: At the Station
qs: Where is the woman going?
When does her train depart?
Which platform is it on?
listening.script: Listen. 'Excuse me, when does the next train to Bukhara depart?' 'At 2:15, from platform 4.' 'How long does it take?' 'About five hours.' 'One ticket, please.' 'Here you are. The train arrives in Bukhara at 7:20 in the evening.'

writing.title: Describe a Journey
writing.task: Write about a journey you made: how you travelled, how long it took, what you saw. (5-7 sentences)

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: How do you get to school?
Which is better, plane or train?
Plane is faster, but train is cheaper.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Ask a ticket price and time at a station or online. Report to class. / Bilet narxini so'rang.

lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 transport words 3× · Grammar: 6 sentences about travelling · Reading: re-read 'To Samarkand by Train' · Speaking: plan a journey with your family.
teacher: Use a real timetable for practice.
Watch for 'with bus' instead of 'by bus'.
Link to L63: the airport and station.

lessons.title: At the Airport and Station
warmup: What do you need to board a plane? / Samolyotga chiqish uchun nima kerak?

grammar.rule: **Help phrases:** Where is...? / Can I...? / How long does it take? / What time does it...?
ex: **Can I** take this bag on the plane?

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: Your flight is late. It is: → a) delayed b) on time c) departed

reading.title: First Flight
reading.passage: It was Otabek's first flight. At the airport, he went to the check-in desk and showed his passport. The woman smiled and gave him a boarding pass. 'Your gate is number 7,' she said. Then Otabek went through security and waited near the gate. The flight was on time. When he sat by the window, he looked out — the city got smaller and smaller. It was wonderful!
qs: Where did Otabek go first at the airport?
What did the woman give him?
Which gate was his?
Was the flight on time?

listening.title: Airport Announcements
qs: Which flight is boarding?
What is the gate number?
Why is the other flight delayed?
listening.script: Listen to the announcements. 'Attention, passengers. Flight 402 to Moscow is now boarding at gate 7.' 'Flight 305 to London is delayed by two hours because of the weather.' 'Passengers of flight 118, please go to gate 2.'

writing.title: At the Airport
writing.task: Write a dialogue (4-6 lines) between a passenger and an airport worker.
writing.uz: Yo'lovchi va aeroport xodimi suhbatini yozing.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: What time does the flight depart?
Yes, if it's not too heavy.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Find out how to say these signs in Uzbek: Gate, Customs, Departures. / Belgilarni tarjima qiling.

lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 airport words 3× · Grammar: write the airport dialogue · Reading: re-read 'First Flight' · Speaking: describe the airport to your family.
teacher: Show real airport signs and announcements.
Link to L64: describing the trip itself.

lessons.title: Describing a Trip
goals: 🕰️ Use first, then, after that, finally
warmup: Tell one thing you saw on your last trip. / Oxirgi safarda nima ko'rdingiz?
first → then → finally. What's next? / Tartib so'zlari.

x: Then we walked to the lake.
We had a great view of the city.

grammar.rule: Sequence: **First... Then... After that... Finally...** + past tense

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: Put in order: → a) First-Travelling-Finally b) First-Then-Finally c) Then-First-Finally

reading.title: A Day in Khiva
reading.passage: Last week my class went on a trip to Khiva. First, we left school very early in the morning. The journey by bus took five hours. Then, we walked through the old city. The scenery was amazing — high blue towers and narrow streets. After that, we had lunch at a small café. Finally, we visited the museum and took many photos. It was a tiring but unforgettable day!
qs: When did the class leave?
How long was the bus journey?
What did they see in the old city?
Where did they have lunch?

listening.title: The Mountain Trip
qs: Where did they go?
What did they do first?
What did they see on the mountain?
listening.script: Listen. Last Sunday we went to the mountains. First, we drove for two hours. Then we walked up the mountain. The view from the top was amazing — green valleys and white clouds below us. After that, we had a picnic. Finally, we came down and drove home. What a day!

writing.title: Describe a Trip
writing.task: Write about a trip (6-8 sentences) using: first, then, after that, finally.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: First we walked through the city.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Tell a family member about a trip using first/then/finally. / Safarni tartib bilan aytib bering.

lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 sequence words 3× · Grammar: write a trip paragraph · Reading: re-read 'A Day in Khiva' · Speaking: describe a trip to your family.
teacher: Use photos from trips to spark storytelling.
Drill sequence words — order is the key skill.
This is a core speaking skill for the whole band.

lessons.title: Comparing Cities
warmup: Name 5 things you find in a big city. / Katta shaharda nimalar bor?
Tashkent vs Samarkand — which is bigger? / Qaysi katta?

x: My grandmother lives in a village.
The population is about three million.
The bazaar is crowded on Sunday.
The traffic is heavy at 8 am.
Bukhara is one of the oldest cities.

grammar.rule: Comparative: **-er / more + than** · Superlative: **the -est / the most**
ex: Tashkent is **the biggest** city in Uzbekistan.

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: This city is ___ (busy) than our village.
It is the ___ (interesting) place I know.

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: Bukhara is one of ___ cities. → a) the oldest b) older c) more old

reading.title: Two Lives
reading.passage: Aziza lives in Tashkent, and her cousin Bek lives in a village near Andijan. Tashkent is bigger and busier than the village. It has more schools, shops and hospitals, but the traffic is heavy. In the village, life is quieter. Bek says the air is cleaner and people are friendlier. 'The village is cheaper and calmer,' he says. 'But I love visiting Tashkent for the cinemas and parks.' Both places are special — in different ways.
qs: Where does Bek live?
What does Tashkent have more of?
What does Bek like about the village?
What does Aziza's cousin like about Tashkent?

listening.title: City or Village?
qs: Why does the woman prefer the village?
Why does the man prefer the city?
Where do they both agree food is cheaper?
listening.script: Listen. Woman: 'I love the village. It's quieter and the air is cleaner.' Man: 'But the city has more jobs and better schools.' Woman: 'True, but food is cheaper in the village.' Man: 'And transport is better in the city. Every place has good and bad points!'

writing.title: My Town vs Another Town
writing.task: Write 5 sentences comparing your town with another place: size, age, traffic, prices, nature.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: Which is bigger, your town or Tashkent?
I prefer the city because of the cinemas.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Compare two places you know and share your opinion with your family. / Ikkita joyni taqqoslang.

lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 city words 3× · Grammar: 6 comparisons + superlatives · Reading: re-read 'Two Lives' · Speaking: discuss your town with your family.
teacher: Use a map of Uzbekistan to compare cities.

lessons.title: Cultural Traditions
warmup: Name 2 traditions: weddings? tea? / O'zbek an'analarini ayting.
Do you know a tradition from another country? / Boshqa xalq an'anasi?

x: I love learning about different cultures.
It is a custom to greet elders first.
Hospitality is important in our culture.
We show respect to our elders.
They celebrate this day with music.
Traditions are passed down to children.
Chet ellik mehmonlar har doim kutib olinadi.

grammar.rule: **It is a custom/tradition to + verb** · describing what people usually do
grammar.uz: 'It is a tradition to...' — an'ana haqida
ex: **It is a custom to** greet elders first.
Odamlar odatda mehmonlar bilan ovqat bo'lishadi.
**Traditions are passed down** from parents to children.
mistake: Wrong: *It is tradition to eat plov.*
Right: *It is a tradition to eat plov.*

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: It is ___ custom to greet elders. (a/the)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: Hospitality means: → a) being kind to guests b) being late c) buying gifts

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: a / It / to / tradition / plov / is / cook / .

reading.title: An Uzbek Wedding
reading.passage: An Uzbek wedding is a joyful celebration full of traditions. First, the groom's family comes to the bride's house with gifts. Then everyone goes to the wedding hall. There is a ceremony called 'kelin salom' — the bride greets the guests and bows respectfully. People eat plov, dance and play music late into the night. The traditions are passed down from grandparents to children. Hospitality and respect are at the heart of every celebration.
qs: What do the groom's family bring?
What happens in the 'kelin salom' ceremony?
What do people eat at the wedding?
What is at the heart of Uzbek celebrations?

listening.title: Traditions Around the World
qs: What happens in Japan?
What do people do in Italy?
Which tradition surprises the speaker?
listening.script: Listen. Around the world, traditions are different. In Japan, people bow when they greet each other. In Italy, people celebrate the New Year with fireworks and wear red. In Mexico, the family makes a special dinner on the Day of the Dead. Traditions are beautiful because they are different — that is what makes the world interesting.

writing.title: A Tradition I Love
writing.task: Write a paragraph (5-7 sentences) about a tradition in your family or country.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: What is a tradition in your family?
We always have plov on Fridays.
How do you show respect to elders?
We greet them first and stand up.
They connect us to our past.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Ask your grandparents about a tradition from their time. Tell the class. / Buvilardan an'ana so'rang.

quiz: Fill: 'It is ___ tradition to greet guests.' (a/the)
lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 tradition words 3× · Grammar: 6 sentences about traditions · Reading: re-read 'An Uzbek Wedding' · Speaking: explain a tradition to your family.
teacher: Invite students to share family traditions — cultural pride.
Drill 'It is a tradition/custom to + verb'.

lessons.title: Class Trip Workshop
goals: 🗣️ Present and vote on the plan
Rejani taqdim etish va ovoz berish
warmup: Name 3 places your class could visit. / Sinf qayerga borishi mumkin?
How much does a bus trip cost? / Avtobus qancha turadi?

x: We are planning a class trip.
Our budget is 50,000 som per person.
A guide will show us around.

practice.title: Plan the Trip
items: Choose a place and say why it is interesting. / Joy tanlang va sababini ayting.
Choose transport and estimate the cost. / Transport va narxni hisoblang.
Make a schedule: 'First we... Then we... Finally we...' / Dastur tuzing.
Check the budget: entrance fees, food, transport. / Byudjetni tekshiring.
Present your plan — the class votes! / Rejani taqdim eting.

speaking.title: Present Your Plan
speaking.body: Present your trip: place, transport, schedule, budget. (5-7 sentences) / Sayohat rejangizni taqdim eting.

speaking.title: Persuade Me
speaking.body: Convince your partner your trip is the best: 'It's more interesting than... / cheaper than...'. / Rejangiz eng yaxshiligini isbotlang.

speaking.title: Class Vote
speaking.body: The class votes for one trip. The winner becomes the real plan! / Sinf ovoz bersin.

lessons.homework: Write a one-paragraph proposal for your dream class trip. / Orzu qilingan sayohat taklifini yozing.

lessons.title: Speaking Circle: Holiday
goals: ☀️ Narrate a holiday in the past
warmup: Tell one thing you did on your last holiday. / Oxirgi dam olishda nima qildingiz?
went, saw, ate, visited — quick drill. / O'tgan zamonni takrorlang.

practice.title: Holiday Discussion Cards
items: Where did you go on your last holiday? / Qayerga bordingiz?
Who did you go with? / Kim bilan bordingiz?
What was the best moment? / Eng yaxshi lahza?
What did you eat? / Nima yedingiz?
Was it relaxing or exciting? Why? / Tinchmi yoki hayajonlimi?

speaking.title: My Holiday
speaking.body: Speak for 2 minutes about your holiday: place, people, food, best moment. / Dam olishingiz haqida gapiring.

speaking.title: Interview
table: I went to my grandparents' village.

speaking.title: Active Listening
speaking.body: Write 3 things your partner did on holiday. / Juftingizning 3 ta ishini yozing.

lessons.homework: Write your holiday story (8-10 sentences). Practice speaking it. / Dam olish hikoyangizni yozing.
teacher: Prompt with photos to spark memories.
Collect great stories to celebrate progress.

lessons.title: Healthy Habits
goals: 🍎 Talk about healthy and unhealthy habits
warmup: Is eating sweets every day healthy? / Har kuni shirinlik yeyish sog'lommi?
Name 3 healthy habits. / 3 ta sog'lom odat ayting.

x: You shouldn't eat late at night.

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: Advice for a cold: → a) You should rest b) You should run c) You shouldn't sleep

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: shouldn't / You / sugar / eat / too / much / .

reading.title: A Healthier Me
reading.passage: Last month, Sardor felt tired every day. His doctor said: 'You should sleep more and eat better.' So Sardor made a plan. He started to eat fresh fruit and vegetables. He drank more water and less cola. He exercised for thirty minutes every day. Now Sardor has more energy. 'I feel great!' he says. 'Small healthy habits changed my life.'
qs: Why did Sardor see a doctor?
What did the doctor say?
What did Sardor change?
How does he feel now?

listening.title: Health Advice
qs: What should the boy eat?
What shouldn't he do at night?
What should he do every day?
listening.script: Listen. 'Hello, doctor.' 'Hello, what's the problem?' 'I feel sleepy all the time.' 'You should eat a good breakfast and drink more water. You shouldn't use your phone late at night. You should exercise every day. Then you will feel better!'

writing.title: My Healthy Plan
writing.task: Write 5 pieces of advice for a healthy day using should/shouldn't.
writing.uz: Sog'lom kun uchun 5 ta maslahat yozing.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: What should I eat for breakfast?
You should eat eggs and bread.
What shouldn't I do before bed?

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Give one piece of health advice to each family member today. / Oilangizga maslahat bering.

lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 health words 3× · Grammar: 6 should/shouldn't sentences · Reading: re-read 'A Healthier Me' · Speaking: share your healthy plan with your family.
teacher: Give real advice about students' habits.
Link to L71-73: health problems and the doctor.

lessons.title: Feelings and Emotions
goals: 🗣️ Say how you feel and why
Qanday his qilayotganingizni va sababini aytish
🤝 Ask and care about others' feelings
warmup: Show a feeling — students guess! / Hisni imo bilan ko'rsating.
Tell the class in English. / Bugun kayfiyatingiz qanday?

x: She felt sad about the news.
I was nervous before the test.
We are excited about the trip!
My parents are proud of me.
She is worried about the exam.
We were surprised by the gift.

grammar.rule: Feelings with **am/is/are + adjective** · **feel + adjective** · reasons with **because**
ex: I **am happy because** I passed the test.
mistake: Wrong: *I am very happy because of I...*

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: You feel before a big test: → a) nervous b) calm c) bored

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: am / happy / I / because / test / passed / I / .
about / the / trip / excited / We / are / .

reading.title: A Big Surprise
reading.passage: Today was an exciting day. In the morning, I felt nervous because we had a maths test. I studied hard all week, so I was calm. After the test, my teacher smiled and said: 'Well done!' I felt proud and happy. When I came home, my family was waiting for me. 'Surprise!' they shouted — they had prepared my favourite dinner. I was so surprised and happy. It was a perfect day.
qs: Why was the writer nervous in the morning?
How did he feel after the test?
What did the family prepare?
How did he feel at the end?

listening.title: How Do They Feel?
qs: Why is Lola sad?
Why is Umid angry?
Why is Bobur excited?
listening.script: Listen. Lola is sad because her best friend moved to another city. Umid is angry because his brother broke his new phone. Bobur is excited because tomorrow he is going on a trip with his class. Everyone has different feelings today.

writing.title: How I Felt
writing.task: Write about a day when you felt happy, nervous or proud (5-7 sentences). Say why.
writing.uz: Qachondir qanday his qilganingiz haqida yozing.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Ask 3 people how they feel today. Report to class. / 3 kishidan kayfiyatini so'rang.

lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 feelings 3× · Grammar: 6 sentences about feelings + because · Reading: re-read 'A Big Surprise' · Speaking: talk about feelings with your family.
teacher: Feelings mime is a great warmer.
This prepares L71-73: health and the doctor.
